recipes.name: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients_raw: 12 Anaheim chile peppers, charred and peeled
1 pound Cheddar cheese, cut into strips

steps.text: Remove seeds and membranes from chile peppers. Stuff each pepper with a strip of Cheddar.
Mix milk, 1 cup flour, egg, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and 1 teaspoon canola oil together in a small bowl until well combined. Place remaining 1/2 cup flour on a shallow plate.
Pour 1 inch oil into a heavy frying pan. Heat over medium-high heat.
Roll each pepper in flour, then dip in batter. Fry in batches until lightly browned on both sides.

raw_recipe.headline: Chiles Rellenos
raw_recipe.description: Delicious chiles rellenos are stuffed with Cheddar cheese, dipped in a simple batter, then fried in canola oil until crispy and golden brown.

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to turn Anaheim peppers into vehicles for cheese! Once we add the cheese into the peppers, we'll dip them into an egg batter and fry until browned and crispy. For a spicier version, try using poblano peppers.

review.reviewBody: This was the best and easiest recipe for rellenos, I tweaked it just a little and instead of going thru the hassle of cutting the cheese, I used string cheese, the combo stick with cheddar and mozzarella cheese, I sliced it in ½ (long way) and with that, I was able to get 2 rellenos out of one stick, it fries nicely and it doesn’t splatter like some cheeses do.. I made a tomato gravy type sauce to pour over the rellenos, that calls for one can of diced tomato with juice, 3 finely chopped celery sticks, ½ cup finely chopped onions, 2 finely chopped fresh jalapenos (remove seeds and membrane) and handful of chopped cilantro, sauté celery, onions, and jalapenos till soft, let cool and pour into blender, add the can of diced tomatoes, cilantro and blend till smooth, season with garlic salt and pepper to taste, Just pour the amount you want over the rellenos,

I have tried many different chile rellenos recipes, and this batter is fabulous, better than going to the hassle of using a lot of egg whites, and the result is excellent. 

 I used 6 poblano peppers (broiled, charred, peeled, seeds removed). I used two kinds of Mexican cheese (sliced 1/2" x 2" firm Casero (white) cheese and a spoonful of Requezo (similar to ricotta). Great flavor and the Requezo helps seal the peppers. Then I rolled them in flour. 

 The batter was too thick to dip the peppers, so I spread a layer of batter on one side of the pepper, then dropped the battered side of the pepper in the hot oil (I only use about 1/4" of oil). I then spread a layer of batter on the other side while the pepper browned. They came out light and fluffy. I kept them warm in the oven at 350 degrees til all six were done. I used a can of enchilada sauce, thickened with some cornstarch and water, for the sauce. Thank you for this great recipe, it's a keeper!

I beat egg whites and then yolks separately and fold into whites. To speed up the process, canned whole green chilies works well for a weeknight meal. Also, instead of dipping chili in egg batter, put a little oil in a skillet (you don't need it an inch deep), heat, then put a line of the egg, kind of the shape of the chili in the pan, let it cook just a bit to start to set up, place the chili on top of the egg, then put more egg over the top of the chili. You end up with nice coverage of the pepper. One more tip. We used to have a restaurant in our town that made crab chili rellenos. Along with the cheese (monterey jack or pepper jack), insert a little crab in each one. Yummy!

This is my first review. Thanks for the recipe PANCHITA! I cheated a little bit and used the leftover canned green chile’s I had from another recipe. I also followed the advice of a few others and whipped my egg whites before adding them to the rest of the batter ingredients. The batter fried up light and crispy on the outside, soft and pillowy on the inside. I even used the extra batter on some veggies ie sweet potatoes, asparagus, zucchini etc. Will definitely make again!

Excellent recipe! Being an old native of New Mexico and lover of Hatch Chiles. This was like old home week. I have used Cheddar cheese but, love Cotijo or Asadero also. I would like to submit a method of blistering the peppers that works like a charm for us. Get a small propane torch, and blister the peppers outside on your bbq grill, laying them on the grill and turning them with tongs until black. Use the tongs to put them in a plastic bag while still warm and seal it. Place them in the freezer and when you are ready to cook them, take them out of the bag one by one and hold them under the faucet with cool running water. The skin slides right off. Pat them dry and follow the recipe…

This is a very authentic recipe. It came out very well and tasted just fabulous, using super fresh chiles and super fresh queso fresco. I have to admit, it was one of the hardest dishes I have ever made. It's labor intensive, and frying the chiles with the fluffy batter takes some skill. My changes: I agree with another cook, clean out the seeds and membranes of the chiles before roasting. I tried it both ways, since i had a dozen chiles to make, and the pre-cleaned chiles were done quickly. The chiles that were not pre-cleaned were easier to get the skins off, but took double the time to very carefully clean out the seeds and membranes, and the water does wash away flavor. They are so delicate once they're cooked! 
I also doubled the batter recipe. I added a good amount of salt to the flour , based on the comments of other cooks, so the end result was flavorful. The batter was a lot of work to beat those egg whites, but SOOOO worth it! I ran out of the egg batter with the last 3 chiles, so I basically just used the dusting flour with the remaining liquid egg and those turned out ok. Next time, for a dozen chiles, I will use 5 eggs so there will be enough batter. Also, the technique for coating the chiles with just the right amount of fluffy batter takes a minute to get the hang of. You have to move quickly and gently, or they will be smothered. That's probably why I ran out at the end. The first few were over-battered, due to my lack of skill. Overall

Okay! Finally a relleno that looks like a proper relleno! I am Mexican and this is how my mother and grandmother made their chiles rellenos and how I make mine. And we all use Anaheim chiles and sharp cheddar cheese. The only difference is we salt the flour, dredge the chiles in it and pat off the excess. Depending on how many chiles you are frying, you separate your eggs. Whip up the whites, fold in the yolks, dip your chiles in the batter and fry. They are labor intensive and absolutely worth it. If you follow this recipe, you will be making rellenos autenticos.

this recipe fails to mention that you need to soften the peppers. to do that I broil them until they're charred. then I put them in a sealed plastic Ziploc bag. and beat the egg and milk to soft peaks. fold into the flour mixture. this is the authentic way of making these. i use poblano peppers over the Anaheim. they're spicier.

We always use Jack Cheese in our rellenos. Most of the time we use the canned chili’s. Rinse them and pate dry. Most important part is to roll chilies in flour or the batter will not stick to the chilies. And like most here have noted , beat the egg whites until stiff then fold in the yokes.

I didn’t dip it in dry flower first but I seasoned the flour mix with garlic, cumin, chili powder and black pepper then fried it and it was a perfect texture and wonderful flavor for true authentic Mexican food

Here's some tips that might help you:
-- use toothpicks to help keep the cheese inside
-- then dip in the batter (making sure you separated the egg white/yolk and whipped whites to soft peaks)

--> Someone please explain how to broil then "steam" the skins... broiling alone didn't seem to do the trick.

--> I fried my first batch, and will bake the second batch, in the oven like a casserole, keeping the chiles separate.

--> I used passilla chiles and queso cheese (this kind of cheese doesn't "liquify" at higher temps).

--> Like tamales, these are time intensive, so make them with a friend!

Please note: you have to roast the peppers and remove the seeds....... not mentioned in the recipe. Still a great batter and flavor. We made a homemade Colorado green chili sauce to pour over and it was amazing. Next time I'll make sure to peel the peppers.
The family enjoyed it. Great recipe.
The batter is great! I’ve been looking for the right type of batter, and this is it!
Tweaked the recipe for the batter a little bit with some minced garlic cumin and chili powder came out great.

Do not agree with using Cheddar Cheese or Red sauce. So much better with Monterrey Jack cheese and a green Chile sauce. More authentic! The batter recipe is good. I also used Bug Jim’s and 1094’s instead of Anaheim.
I need instructions on how to put the cheese in…. Lol!! I thought it tasted good. My husband wants me to add more flavor. I’ll try garlic and?
We always add a strip of round of steak inside with the cheese.
Highly requested at this ranch.
Delicious! Absolutely love this recipe!
